title: Related Rates of Volume Change in a Cylinder
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: The radius of a cylinder increases at dr/dt = 2 cm/s while height decreases at dh/dt = -3 cm/s. Find the rate of volume change dV/dt when r = 10 cm and h = 20 cm.

steps.title: State Volume Formula and Partial Derivatives
steps.mathExpression: V = \pi r^2 h \implies \frac{\partial V}{\partial r} = 2\pi r h, \quad \frac{\partial V}{\partial h} = \pi r^2
steps.explanation: Differentiate cylindrical volume with respect to radius and height.

steps.title: Apply Chain Rule for Total Time Derivative
steps.mathExpression: \frac{dV}{dt} = \frac{\partial V}{\partial r}\frac{dr}{dt} + \frac{\partial V}{\partial h}\frac{dh}{dt} = (2\pi r h)(2) + (\pi r^2)(-3)
steps.explanation: Sum contributions from expanding radius and contracting height.
